entities.summary: Paolo Uccello, born Paolo di Dono, was an Italian Renaissance painter and mathematician from Florence who was notable for his pioneering work on visual perspective in art. In his book Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects, Giorgio Vasari wrote that Uccello was obsessed by his interest in perspective and would stay up all night in his study trying to grasp the exact vanishing point. Uccello used perspective to create a feeling of depth in his paintings. His best known works are the three paintings representing the battle of San Romano, which were wrongly entitled the Battle of Sant'Egidio of 1416 for a long period of time.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Paolo Uccello's pioneering work on visual perspective in art had a significant regional impact, influencing the development of Renaissance art and architecture. His use of perspective created a sense of depth in his paintings, which was a major innovation in the field.
